steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: AQA 8236 requires students to study specific set professional works for the written exam

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The set professional works are 'Within Her Eyes' by James Cousins, 'Artificial Things' by Lucy Bennett and 'Emancipation of Expressionism' by Kenrick H2O Sandy

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Each work has a distinct choreographic intention, style and set of features that must be understood in detail

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Professional works are assessed in Section C of the written exam, worth 25 marks

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: Name the three AQA set professional works and their choreographers. | Q: Which professional work was created for an integrated dance company? | Q: In which section of the written exam are professional works assessed?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: 'Within Her Eyes' by James Cousins, 'Artificial Things' by Lucy Bennett and 'Emancipation of Expressionism' by Kenrick H2O Sandy. | 'Artificial Things' by Lucy Bennett, created for Stopgap Dance Company which features both disabled and non-disabled dancers. | Section C of the AQA 8236 written exam, worth 25 marks.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Learn the basic facts for each work cold: choreographer, company, year, intention, stimulus and structure In Section C, always name the specific work and choreographer — do not write vaguely about 'the dance' Prepare detailed notes on movement content, design elements and choreographic features for each work Practise comparing works — exam questions may ask you to discuss more than one work Use specific examples from each work rather than general statements — detail scores marks
